body:
Create functionality to automatically generate GitHub issues from acceptance criteria with proper naming conventions.

## Problem
Currently creating placeholder issues that don't provide value. Need structured approach to generate meaningful issues from acceptance criteria.

## Solution
Implement system to create issues with format:
- Title: `<short issue description (30 char max)>: AC <short acceptance criteria (50 char max)>`
- Body: Detailed acceptance criteria and context
- Proper labeling: "feature" for new issues, "ac" for acceptance criteria
- One issue per acceptance criterion (no breaking up TDD cycles)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Create script/function to parse acceptance criteria
- [ ] Generate issues with proper title format (30/50 char limits)  
- [ ] Include detailed acceptance criteria in issue body
- [ ] Add "feature" label to new issues with defined AC
- [ ] Add "ac" label to acceptance criteria issues
- [ ] Generate one issue per acceptance criterion
- [ ] Integrate with existing WorkFlo workflow
- [ ] Add validation for title length constraints
- [ ] Handle duplicate issue prevention

## Implementation Notes
- Replace current non-interactive issue creation
- Ensure issues are actionable and trackable
- Maintain consistency with project standards
- Keep TDD cycles intact - one issue per AC
title: Auto-generate issues from acceptance criteria

body:
The WorkFlo system currently has interactive prompts that break automation and scripting. All commands should be fully command-line driven with parameters and flags. This includes board creation, TDD workflows, and any other user input requests. Interactive prompts make the system unusable in CI/CD pipelines and automated workflows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Remove interactive prompts from board create command
- [ ] Make all board operations command-line driven with parameters
- [ ] Remove interactive inputs from TDD workflow commands
- [ ] Add command-line flags for all user inputs
- [ ] Ensure all commands work in non-interactive/scripted environments
- [ ] Update help documentation to show command-line syntax only
title: Remove all interactivity and replace with command-line only interface

- `tdd-cycle.sh` (546 lines) - Full cycle management

- `tdd-auto-cycle.sh` - Automated cycling
- `tdd-check-cycle.sh` - Validation only


- ✅ **Easier testing** with modular subcommands

## 🎯 Problem Statement

Currently, WorkFlo Windows users must manually check for updates and reinstall the entire application. This creates several issues:

- **Update Friction**: Users avoid updates due to complex manual process
- **Security Risk**: Users stay on outdated versions with potential vulnerabilities  
- **Support Burden**: Multiple versions in use make troubleshooting difficult
- **Feature Adoption**: New features reach users slowly

## 🚀 Proposed Solution

Implement an automated update system using industry-standard solutions:

### Primary Stack:
1. **GitHub Releases** - Primary distribution mechanism
2. **AutoUpdater.NET** - Built-in update checking for .NET applications
3. **Chocolatey** - Package manager for enterprise environments
4. **Windows Package Manager (winget)** - Modern Windows 10/11 integration

### Architecture:
```
[WorkFlo App] → [Update Checker] → [GitHub Releases API]
                       ↓
[Download Manager] → [Delta Updates] → [Background Install]
```

## 📋 Implementation Phases

### Phase 1: GitHub Releases Integration (Week 1-2)
- Set up automated release publishing from CI/CD
- Create release notes generation from commit history
- Implement basic version checking in CLI/API
- Add manual update command: `workflo update`

### Phase 2: AutoUpdater.NET Integration (Week 3-4)
- Add AutoUpdater.NET NuGet package to CLI and API projects
- Implement background update checking (daily)
- Create update notification system
- Add user consent flow for updates

### Phase 3: Package Manager Distribution (Week 5-6)
- Submit to Chocolatey community repository
- Create winget manifest for Windows Package Manager
- Set up automated package publishing

### Phase 4: Advanced Features (Week 7-8)
- Implement delta updates (download only changes)
- Add rollback capability
- Create update channel system (stable/beta)
- Add enterprise deployment options

## ✅ Acceptance Criteria

**Must Have:**
- [ ] Users receive automatic update notifications
- [ ] Updates can be installed without admin privileges (where possible)
- [ ] Update process preserves user data and configuration
- [ ] Failed updates can be rolled back
- [ ] Update checking can be disabled via configuration

**Should Have:**
- [ ] Delta updates to reduce download size
- [ ] Background downloads with user consent
- [ ] Update channels (stable/beta) for different user needs
- [ ] Enterprise deployment via package managers

**Nice to Have:**
- [ ] Automatic updates with user consent
- [ ] Update analytics and metrics
- [ ] Custom update server for enterprise environments

## 🔧 Technical Specifications

### Update Manifest Format:
All updates will use a JSON manifest with version info, download URLs, checksums, and metadata for security verification.

### Security Considerations:
- All updates must be code-signed
- HTTPS-only distribution
- Checksum verification before installation
- Rollback on installation failure

### Configuration Options:
Users can configure update behavior including enabling/disabling updates, channels, and notification preferences.

## 🔗 Dependencies

### External Libraries:
- **AutoUpdater.NET** (MIT License) - .NET update framework
- **Newtonsoft.Json** (MIT License) - JSON parsing
- **System.IO.Compression** (Built-in) - Archive handling

### Services:
- **GitHub Releases API** - Release metadata and downloads
- **GitHub Actions** - Automated release publishing
- **Code Signing Certificate** - Windows executable signing

## 🧪 Testing Strategy

### Unit Tests:
- Update checking logic
- Version comparison algorithms
- Configuration management
- Error handling scenarios

### Integration Tests:
- GitHub API integration
- Download and installation process
- Rollback functionality
- Package manager integration

### Manual Testing:
- End-to-end update flow on clean Windows systems
- Network failure scenarios
- Disk space limitations
- Antivirus interaction testing

## 🎯 Success Metrics

- **User Adoption**: >80% of users on latest version within 30 days
- **Update Success Rate**: >95% successful updates
- **Support Reduction**: <50% fewer version-related support requests
- **Security**: 0 days between security fix and user deployment

## 🔄 Alternative Solutions Considered

### Rejected Options:
1. **ClickOnce Deployment** - Limited to .NET Framework, poor user experience
2. **Microsoft Store** - Complex approval process, distribution limitations
3. **Custom Update Server** - High maintenance overhead, reinventing wheel
4. **Installer Frameworks** - Complex, overengineered for our needs

### Future Considerations:
1. **Electron Auto-updater** - If we move to Electron for UI
2. **Squirrel.Windows** - Alternative to AutoUpdater.NET
3. **Windows Store** - Long-term distribution channel

## 🏷️ Labels and Priority

**Suggested Priority**: High
**Category**: Feature Enhancement
**Components**: Windows, Distribution, User Experience
**Effort**: Large (6-8 weeks)
**Risk**: Medium (external dependencies)
